questions.q: The absolute difference of the coefficients of $x^{10}$~and $x^{7}$~in the expansion of \left(2x^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2x}\right)11$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given expansion is& \left(2x^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2x}\right)11$.

The~general term in the binomial expansion of~\left(x + a\right)n$~is given by~${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n x^{n - r}a^{r}$.

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = Cr 11 \left(2x^{2}\right)11 - r\left(\dfrac{1}{2x}\right)r$

$= Cr 11 \left({2}^{11 - r - r}\right)x^{22 - 2r - r}$

Now for coefficient~of~$x^{7}⇒ 22 - 3r = 7$

$⇒ r = 5$

Coefficient of~$x^{7}$~is~$C5 11 \left({2}^{11 - 5 \times 2}\right)

Now for coefficient of~$x^{10} ⇒ 22 - 3r = 10$

$⇒ r = 4$

Coefficient of~$x^{10}$~is~$C4 11 \left({2}^{11 - 2 \times 4}\right)$

We need the absolute difference, we get it by~\left|C5 11 \left({2}^{11 - 5 \times 2}\right) - C4 11 \left({2}^{11 - 4 \times 2}\right)\right|$.

$= \left|924 - 2640\right| = 1716$

$= {12}^{3} - 12$

Hence the absolute difference~is~$= {12}^{3} - 12.

$

questions.solution:
Total number of terms in the expansion of& \left(2\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{2\left(3\right)\dfrac{1}{3}}\right)10 = 10 + 1 = 11$

Now,~${5}^{th}$~term from end~$= 11 - 5 + 1 = {7}^{th}$~from beginning.

We need to find a~ratio of the ${5}^{th}$ term from the beginning to the ${5}^{th}$ term from the end (i.e.~${7}^{th}$~term from beginning)~in the binomial expansion of \left(2\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{2\left(3\right)\dfrac{1}{3}}\right)10 = \dfrac{T5}{T7}$

$= \dfrac{10{C}_{4}\left(2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)10 - 4 \left(\dfrac{1}{2 \left($3\$right)\dfrac{1}{3}}\$right)4}{10{C}_{6}\$lleft(2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)$10 - 6 $\$left(\dfrac{1}{2 \left(3\$right)\dfrac{1}{3}}\right)$6} \left[$∵ {T}_{r + 1}{=}^{n}{C}_{r} \left(a\right)n - r\left(b\right)r\right]$

$= $\dfrac{\left(10 !\right)\left(4 !\right)\left(6 !\right) \times \left(2\right)2 \times \dfrac{1}{\left({2}^{4}\right)\left(3\right)\dfrac{4}{3}}}{\left(10 !\right)\left(6 !\right)\left(4 !\right) \times \left(2\right)\dfrac{4}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{\left({2}^{6}\right)\left(3\right)2}}

$= 4\left(36\right)\dfrac{1}{3}: 1$

$

questions.solution:
Given,

${25}^{190} - {19}^{190} - {8}^{190} + {2}^{190}$

Now \left({25}^{190} - {19}^{190}\right), {8}^{190}, {2}^{190}$ are divisible by $2$, as~${25}^{190}$~will give remainder as $1$~and~${19}^{190}$~will give remainder as $1$~when~divided~by~$2$, so combined~${25}^{190} - {19}^{190}$~will give remainder~$0$~

Now,~\left({25}^{190} - {8}^{190}\right) \text{ and } \left(- {19}^{190} + {2}^{190}\right) are divisible by $17$,~$a^{n} - b^{n}$~is divisible by~$a - b$~if~$n$~is even,~
So given number is divisible by~$34$~as it is divisible by~$2 & 17$~both,

Now,${25}^{190} = \left($7 $\times$3 + 4\right)190$, dividing by~$7$~we get,

\left($7 $\times$3 + 4\right)190 = {4}^{190} = {16}^{95} = {2}^{95} = 4 $\cdot {8}^{31}

Now when~$4 $\cdot \left($7 + 1\right)31$~divided by~$7$~will give remainder as~$4 $\cdot$1 = 4$

And~${19}^{190} = \left($7 $\times$3 - 2\right)190$, when divided by~$7$~we get,

\left($7 $\times$3 - 2\right)190 = \left(-$2\right)190 = {2}^{190} = 2 $\times {8}^{63} =$2 $\times \left($7 + 1\right)63$

Similarly~${8}^{190} = \left($7 + 1\right)190$~will give~$1$~remainder~

And~${2}^{190} = 2\left($7 + 1\right)63$~will give~$1$~remainder,

questions.q: If for some positive integer $n$, the coefficients of three consecutive terms in the binomial expansion of \left(1 + x\right)n + 5$ are in the ratio $5: 10: 14$, then the largest coefficient in the expansion is :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let three consecutive terms are ${T}_{r}, {T}_{r + 1}, {T}_{r + 2}$
So,~$\dfrac{Cr - 1 n + 5}{Cr n + 5} = \dfrac{5}{10}$~and~$\dfrac{Cr n + 5}{Cr + 1 n + 5} = \dfrac{10}{14}$

Using property~$\dfrac{Cr n}{Cr - 1 n} = \dfrac{n - r + 1}{r}$, we have

$\dfrac{\left(n + 5\right) - r + 1}{r} = 2$~and~$\dfrac{\left(n + 5\right) - \left(r + 1\right) + 1}{r + 1} = \dfrac{7}{5}$

$⇒ n - 3r + 6 = 0$~and~$5n - 12r + 18 = 0$

Solving both equations,~$n = 6, r = 4$
Hence, the greatest coefficient will be of middle term, which is~$= C5 n + 5 = C5 11 = 462$

If the ratio of the fifth term from the beginning to the fifth term from the end in the expansion of& \left(24 + \dfrac{1}{34}\right)n$~is~$\sqrt{6}: 1$, \text{ and } then the third term from the beginning is:

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given expansion is\left(24 + \dfrac{1}{34}\right)n$

We know that general term of an expansion~\left(x + a\right)n$~is~${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n x^{n - r}a^{r}$

(${5}^{th}$~term from beginning)

${T}_{4 + 1} = C4 n ( 24 {)}^{n - 4} \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{34}\right)4$

(${5}^{th}$~term from end)

We know~that~$r$th term from the end in a binomial expansion is~${T}_{n - r + 2}$~from the beginning.

${T}_{5}^{'} = {T}_{n - 4 + 1} = C4 n \left(\dfrac{1}{34}\right)n - 4 ( 24 {)}^{4}$

It is also given that the ratio of~the fifth term from the beginning to the fifth term from the end is~$\sqrt{6}: 1$.

Now,~${T}_{5}{T}_{5}^{'} = \dfrac{6}{1}$

$⇒ 2\dfrac{n - 8}{4} \cdot 3\dfrac{n - 8}{4} = \sqrt{6}$

$∴ ( \sqrt{6}) \dfrac{n - 8}{2} = ( \sqrt{6} )$

$∴ n = 10$

$∴ {T}_{3} = C2 10 \left(24\right)8\left(\dfrac{1}{34}\right)2 = \dfrac{45 \times 4}{3}$

$= 60\sqrt{3}$

Hence, this is the correct option.

questions.q: The sum of the coefficients of three consecutive terms in the binomial expansion of& \left(1 + x\right)n + 2$, which are in the ratio~$1: 3: 5$, is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Ratio of three consecutive terms in the binomial expansion of& \left(1 + x\right)n + 2$~is

~$Cr - 1 n + 2 : Cr n + 2 : Cr + 1 n + 2 : : 1: 3: 5$

So,

$⇒ \dfrac{Cr n + 2}{Cr - 1 n + 2} = \dfrac{3}{1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{n - r + 3}{r} = 3$

$⇒ n + 3 = 4r . . . \left(1\right)$

And,

\dfrac{Cr + 1 n + 2}{Cr n + 2} = \dfrac{5}{3}

$⇒ $\dfrac{n + 2 - r}{r + 1} = \dfrac{5}{3}

$⇒ 3n + 6 - 3r = 5r + 5$

$⇒ 3n + 1 = 8r . . . \left(2\right)$

So,~$3\left(4r - 3\right) + 1 = 8r$

$⇒ 12r - 9 + 1 = 8r$

$⇒ 4r = 8$

$⇒ r = 2$

So,~$n = 5$

Hence, we have

\left(1 + x\right)n + 2 = \left(1 + x\right)7$

Sum of consecutive terms is

$C1 7 + C2 7 + C3 7$

$= 7 + 21 + 35 = 63$

questions.q: A possible value of& $x,$~for which the ninth term in the expansion of \left\{{3}^{\log_{3}\sqrt{{25}^{x - 1} + 7}} + {3}^{\left(- \dfrac{1}{8}\right)\log_{3}\left({5}^{x - 1} + 1\right)}\right\}10$ in the increasing powers of ${3}^{\left(- \dfrac{1}{8}\right)\log_{3}\left({5}^{x - 1} + 1\right)}$ is equal to~$180,$ \text{ and } is :$

questions.solution:
\left\{{3}^{\log_{3}\sqrt{{25}^{x - 1} + 7}} + {3}^{\left(- \dfrac{1}{8}\right)\log_{3}\left({5}^{x - 1} + 1\right)}\right\}10$

$= \left\{\sqrt{{25}^{x - 1} + 7} + \left({5}^{x - 1} + 1\right)\dfrac{- 1}{8}\right\}10,$~using~$a^{n\log_{\mathrm{a}}x} = x^{n}$

Using the formula of the general term in the Binomial theorem for non negative integral index, i.e.,~${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n a^{n - r}b^{r}$~in~\left(a + b\right)n,$~we get, ${T}_{9} = {T}_{8 + 1} = C8 10 \left(25\left(x - 1\right) + 7\right) \times \left(5\left(x - 1\right) + 1\right)- 1 = 180$

$⇒ \dfrac{{25}^{x - 1} + 7}{5\left(x - 1\right) + 1} = 4$

$⇒ \dfrac{t^{2} + 7}{t + 1} = 4,$~taking~$t = {5}^{x - 1}$

$⇒ t^{2} + 7 = 4 \left(t + 1\right)$

$⇒ t^{2} - 4t + 3 = 0$

$⇒ \left(t - 3\$right)\left($t - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ t = 1, 3 ⇒ {5}^{x - 1} = 1 ⇒ {5}^{x - 1} = {5}^{0}$

$⇒ x - 1 = 0$~(one of the possible value).

$⇒ x = 1$

$

questions.q: The remainder, when ${7}^{103}$~is divided by $17,$& is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Using the binomial expansion in& ${7}^{103} = \left({7}^{2}\right)51 \cdot 7 = \left(51 - 2\right)51 \cdot 7$~we get,

\left(51 - 2\right)51 \cdot 7 = 7 \cdot \left(C0 51 {51}^{51} \cdot {2}^{0} -C1 51 {51}^{50} \cdot {2}^{1} + . . . . . . . -C51 51 {2}^{51}\right)$

Now~$51$~is divisible by~$17$, so when above equation is divided by~$17$~we get,~$7 \cdot \left(- {2}^{51}\right)$~as remainder,

Now again using binomial in~$7 \cdot \left(- {2}^{51}\right) = - 56\left({2}^{4}\right)12 = - 56\left(17 - 1\right)12$~we get,

$- 56\left(17 - 1\right)12 = - 56 \left(C0 12 {17}^{12} \cdot {1}^{0} -C1 12 {17}^{11} \cdot {1}^{1} + . . . . . . . +C12 12 {1}^{12}\right)$

Now dividing above equation by~$17$~we get,

\left(-56 \times1\right) \div 17 = - 5$,

Now changing negative remainder to positive we get,~$- 5 + 17 = 12$,

Hence, when~${7}^{103}$~divided by~$17$~gives~$12& as remainder.

$

questions.q: The number of integral terms in the expansion of& \left(3\dfrac{1}{2} + 5\dfrac{1}{4}\right)680$ \text{ and } is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given expansion is& \left(3\dfrac{1}{2} + 5\dfrac{1}{4}\right)680$.

The general term in the expansion~\left(x + a\right)n$~is~${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n \cdot x^{n - r} \cdot a^{r}$

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = Cr 680 \left(3\dfrac{1}{2}\right)680 - r\left(5\dfrac{1}{4}\right)r, 0 \le r \le 680$

$= Cr 680 \left(3\right)\dfrac{680 - r}{2}\left(5\right)\dfrac{r}{4}$

For~\left(3\right)\dfrac{680 - r}{2}\left(5\right)\dfrac{r}{4}$~to be rational~$r$~should be a multiple of~$4$.

$⇒ r = 0, 4, 8, 12, . . . . . 680$

$⇒ {a}_{n} = a + \left(n - 1\right)d$

$⇒ 680 = 0 + \left(n - 1\right)4$

$⇒ n = 171$

That means~$r$~can take~$171$~values.

Hence, the required answer is~$171$.

$

questions.q: The term independent of $x$~in the expansion of \left(\dfrac{x + 1}{x^{2 / 3} - x^{1 / 3} + 1} - \dfrac{x - 1}{x - x^{1 / 2}}\right)10,$~where $x \ne 0, 1$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
\left(\dfrac{x + 1}{x^{2 / 3} - x^{1 / 3} + 1} - \dfrac{x - 1}{x - x^{1 / 2}}\right)10$

\left(\dfrac{\left(x^{1 / 3} + 1\right)\left(x^{2 / 3} - x^{1 / 3} + 1\right)}{x^{2 / 3} - x^{1 / 3} + 1} - \dfrac{\left(x^{1 / 2} + 1\right)\left(x^{1 / 2} - 1\right)}{x^{1 / 2}\left(x^{1 / 2} - 1\right)}\right)10$

$= \left(\left(x^{1 / 3} + 1\right) - \left(\dfrac{x^{1 / 2} + 1}{x1 / 2}\right)\right)10$

$= \left(x^{1 / 3} - \dfrac{1}{x1 / 2}\right)10$

Now the~\left(r + 1\right)th$ Term

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 10 \left(x^{1 / 3}\right)10 - r \cdot \left(- \dfrac{1}{x1 / 2}\right)r$

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 10 \left(x^{1 / 3}\right)10 - r \cdot x^{- r / 2}\left(- 1\right)r$

For independent term

$\dfrac{10 - r}{3} - \dfrac{r}{2} = 0 ⇒ r = 4$

$⇒ {T}_{5} = C4 10 \left(- 1\right)4$

$= \dfrac{10 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 210$
